facts.fact: Azure AI Foundry is now named Microsoft Foundry; the rename was announced at Microsoft Ignite on 2025-11-18 (secondary for the Ignite date) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/ ; https://www.directionsonmicrosoft.com/microsoft-ignite-2025-ten-things-you-need-to-know/)
The Microsoft Foundry docs hub lives at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/ and the old /azure/ai-foundry/ path redirects there (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)
The older Foundry portal is documented separately from Microsoft Foundry as 'Foundry (classic)' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)
Microsoft Foundry is part of Microsoft Azure, with docs under learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/ (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)

Azure AI Services were rebranded as 'Foundry Tools', and Azure Updates item AZ526132 announced the rebrand as generally available (secondary for the Azure Updates item) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/ ; https://mc.merill.net/message/AZ526132)
The Foundry docs hub groups Speech, Translator, Language, Document Intelligence, Content Understanding and Face under 'Foundry Tools' (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)

The Foundry RBAC role `Foundry User` was previously named `Azure AI User`; role IDs and permissions are unchanged (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

The Foundry RBAC role `Foundry Owner` was previously named `Azure AI Owner`; role IDs and permissions are unchanged (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

The Foundry RBAC role `Foundry Account Owner` was previously named `Azure AI Account Owner`; role IDs and permissions are unchanged (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

The Foundry RBAC role `Foundry Project Manager` was previously named `Azure AI Project Manager`; role IDs and permissions are unchanged (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

The old Azure AI role names (Azure AI User, Azure AI Owner, Azure AI Account Owner, Azure AI Project Manager) may still appear while the Foundry role rename rolls out (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Foundry Agent Service is GA (as of 2026-11-14) and offers three agent types: prompt agents (configuration only), voice-based prompt agents (preview, run through Voice Live over WebSocket) and hosted agents (your own code in a container or .zip) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)
Prompt agents are the configuration-only agent type of Foundry Agent Service (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)
Code already running elsewhere can call the Responses API directly as an 'ephemeral agent' in Foundry Agent Service (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)

Foundry Agent Service was in preview from December 2024 and first reached GA in May 2025; MCP tool support was added in June 2025, and the Browser Automation tool (Aug 2025) and Computer Use tool (Sep 2025) arrived as previews (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry-classic/agents/whats-new)
Agents (classic), which use threads, runs and assistants, are deprecated and retire on 2027-03-31 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry-classic/agents/whats-new)

Microsoft's migration guide moves Agents (classic) workloads to the new Responses-based agents: conversations instead of threads, responses instead of runs, and versioned agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry-classic/agents/whats-new)
Connected agents (classic) are not carried into the new Foundry Agent Service (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry-classic/agents/whats-new)
The Azure OpenAI Assistants API retired on 2026-08-26, per secondary sources (unverified) (https://endoflife.ai/article-azure-openai-assistants-retirement)
Microsoft's replacement for the retired Azure OpenAI Assistants API is Foundry Agent Service (unverified) (https://endoflife.ai/article-azure-openai-assistants-retirement)
Hosted agents run agent code in per-session VM-isolated sandboxes, and each session gets a persistent `$HOME` and `/files` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)

Hosted agents support Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Anthropic Agent SDK or custom code, in Python or C# (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)
Each hosted agent gets a dedicated Microsoft Entra agent identity and its own endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)

Hosted-agent sandbox sizes are 0.5 vCPU/1 GiB, 1 vCPU/2 GiB or 2 vCPU/4 GiB; the idle timeout is configurable from 2 to 240 minutes (default 15), and sessions are deleted after 30 days of inactivity, all fixed per agent version (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)
Hosted-agent billing covers CPU and memory across active sessions (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)
Hosted-agent versions are immutable, and an endpoint sends 100% of traffic to one version, with no traffic splitting (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)

Hosted agents expose Responses at `{project_endpoint}/agents/{name}/endpoint/protocols/openai/responses`, Invocations (arbitrary JSON) at `/protocols/invocations`, Invocations WebSocket at `/protocols/invocations_ws`, Activity (bridged automatically for Teams and Microsoft 365) and A2A; the container listens on port 8088 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/cli-agent-development)
Hosted agents expose the A2A protocol alongside Responses, Invocations and Activity (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)
A Foundry toolbox endpoint follows the pattern `{project_endpoint}/toolboxes/{name}/mcp?api-version=v1` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview)

Toolboxes bundle Foundry tools behind one managed MCP-compatible endpoint that any MCP client can use, not only Foundry agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Toolboxes add versioning and promotion, centralized auth, `tool_search`/`call_tool` meta-tools for large tool sets, and Skills (preview) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview)

facts.fact: Foundry Agent Service ships built-in tools: MCP, web search, Azure AI Search, code interpreter, file search, OpenAPI, A2A, browser automation, Fabric IQ, Work IQ, function calling, Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation, SharePoint, Fabric data agent and Azure Functions (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview)

Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation, SharePoint, Fabric data agent and Azure Functions tools can't be placed in a toolbox (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/toolbox-overview)

The Microsoft Copilot harness (preview) is an optional runtime for prompt agents that adds file read/write, shell, web and subagents for multi-step workflows (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)

The Microsoft Copilot harness is limited to a subset of regions and doesn't support BYOM, Foundry Memory, `store: false` or `previous_response_id` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)

Long-running hosted agents are in preview: previews announced in August 2026 cover crash-resilient deployment, human-in-the-loop approval, steering an in-flight turn, stream-with-reconnect and task state management (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/whats-new-foundry)
Foundry 'Routines' are triggers that invoke agents, and an agent optimizer (preview) is also documented (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/whats-new-foundry)

Foundry Memory is a managed long-term memory store in preview that stores user profile, chat summary and procedural memory, used through a memory search tool or the Memory Store APIs (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-memory)
Foundry Memory quotas are 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope and 1,000 search or update requests per minute (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-memory)
Foundry Memory doesn't support VNet integration (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-memory)

The Foundry model catalog has two categories: 'Foundry Models sold by Azure' (including Azure OpenAI, MAI, Grok and DeepSeek) and 'Foundry Models from partners and community' (Anthropic, Cohere, Meta, Mistral, NTT Data and others) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

Partner models in the Foundry catalog are billed through Azure Marketplace, which requires `Microsoft.SaaS/register/action` and MarketplaceOrdering permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)
Foundry partner and community models are billed through Azure Marketplace (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

The Owner and Contributor roles include the `Microsoft.SaaS/register/action` and MarketplaceOrdering permissions needed to buy Foundry partner models (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

The Contributor role includes the `Microsoft.SaaS/register/action` and MarketplaceOrdering permissions needed to buy Foundry partner models (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

Claude models are in the Foundry catalog in two hosting versions, one hosted on Azure and one on Anthropic infrastructure, with possibly different lifecycle status; the catalog lists `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-fable-5-2` and others (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

Claude Global Standard in Foundry is mostly in East US 2 and Sweden Central plus several US regions, and Data Zone Standard (US only) covers some models when hosted on Azure (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

Claude in Foundry does not support CSP subscriptions, Enterprise Agreement accounts in South Korea, or credit-only, sponsored and free-trial subscriptions (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

Several sampling parameters are rejected on newer Claude models in Foundry, for example `temperature` and `top_k`, and `top_p` must be at least 0.99 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners)

'Instant access (preview)' calls supported models by name without a deployment and is separate from the deployment types (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)
Foundry IQ, the managed knowledge layer for agents, is built on Azure AI Search knowledge bases and agentic retrieval (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-foundry-iq)

Foundry IQ supports Blob, SharePoint, OneLake and web sources, ACL sync, Purview labels and queries under the caller's Entra identity; some features are GA and some preview depending on the Search REST API version (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-foundry-iq)

Azure AI Search agentic retrieval uses REST API `2026-04-01` for GA features (GA knowledge source types, minimal extractive retrieval) and `2026-08-01-preview` for LLM query planning, answer synthesis, low or medium reasoning effort and multi-turn messages (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/agentic-retrieval-overview)
The Azure and Foundry portals expose only preview schemas for agentic retrieval (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/agentic-retrieval-overview)

Agentic retrieval bills tokens on two services: Azure AI Search charges retrieval tokens (free monthly allowance, then pay-as-you-go) and Azure OpenAI charges query-planning tokens (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/agentic-retrieval-overview)
Azure OpenAI charges for the query-planning tokens used by Azure AI Search agentic retrieval (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/agentic-retrieval-overview)
Azure AI Search knowledge bases can be queried through a retrieve action or an MCP endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/search/agentic-retrieval-overview)

Foundry tracing uses OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, with integrations for Agent Framework, LangChain, LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/concepts/trace-agent-concept)
Foundry tracing stores trace data in Application Insights (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/concepts/trace-agent-concept)

Foundry tracing is GA for prompt and hosted agents and in preview for workflow and external agents (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/concepts/trace-agent-concept)
Viewing Foundry traces requires a Log Analytics reader role (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/concepts/trace-agent-concept)

facts.fact: Foundry evaluations run through the OpenAI-compatible `client.evals` API, obtained from `AIProjectClient.get_openai_client()` with `azure-ai-projects>=2.8.0` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/evaluate-agent)

Foundry evaluations offer rubric evaluators generated from the agent's context, built-in evaluators (`builtin.violence`, `builtin.coherence` and others), agent targets (`azure_ai_agent`), continuous evaluation and GitHub Actions gates (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/evaluate-agent ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)
An AI Red Teaming Agent is available in preview alongside Foundry evaluations (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/)
Microsoft Agent Framework is the direct successor to Semantic Kernel, built by the same teams, and Microsoft publishes a migration guide (https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/overview/)
Microsoft Agent Framework is the direct successor to AutoGen, built by the same teams, and Microsoft publishes a migration guide (https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/overview/)

Microsoft Agent Framework version 1.0 (GA for .NET and Python) was announced on 2026-04-03, and a Go version is in public preview (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/5212)
The PyPI package `agent-framework` was at 1.26.0 on 2026-11-12 (https://pypi.org/project/agent-framework/)

Agent Framework packages are `agent-framework` (pip) and `Microsoft.Agents.AI` (NuGet), with `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry` adding Foundry support (prerelease); Go uses `github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go` (https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/overview/ ; https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/wp-json/wp/v2/posts/5212)

Microsoft Agent Framework covers agents, a 'Harness Agent', graph-based workflows, MCP clients and model providers including Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama (https://learn.microsoft.com/agent-framework/overview/)

Microsoft has not stated a Semantic Kernel or AutoGen end-of-life date in the pages checked; the Semantic Kernel overview page doesn't mention Agent Framework, and secondary sources call both frameworks 'maintenance mode' (secondary) (https://learn.microsoft.com/semantic-kernel/overview/ ; https://visualstudiomagazine.com/articles/2026/04/06/microsoft-ships-production-ready-agent-framework-1-0-for-net-and-python.aspx)

No AutoGen end-of-life date was found on Microsoft pages; secondary sources call it 'maintenance mode' (secondary) (https://visualstudiomagazine.com/articles/2026/04/06/microsoft-ships-production-ready-agent-framework-1-0-for-net-and-python.aspx)

Azure Logic Apps supports autonomous and conversational agentic workflows, where an 'agent loop' action can use the 1,400+ connectors as tools; agentic workflows are available in Standard and in preview for Consumption (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)

Logic Apps Consumption agent loops use Foundry models, while Standard uses an Azure OpenAI resource, a Foundry project (preview) or an APIM LLM API (preview) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)
In Logic Apps agentic workflows an agent can't be nested as a tool inside another agent (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)

Production chat clients for Logic Apps agentic workflows need Easy Auth (Standard) or OAuth 2.0 with Entra ID (Consumption), because the portal 'developer key' is for testing only (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)
Logic Apps Consumption agentic workflow chat clients use OAuth 2.0 with Entra ID in production (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)
Logic Apps Consumption agent loops bill tokens as Enterprise Units (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/agent-workflows-concepts)

Microsoft Fabric data agents are GA and answer natural-language questions over lakehouses, warehouses, Power BI semantic models, KQL databases (Eventhouse), mirrored databases, ontologies and Microsoft Graph by generating NL2SQL, NL2DAX and NL2KQL queries (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/concept-data-agent)

facts.target: Microsoft Fabric F2+ or P1+ capacity
facts.fact: Fabric data agents need an F2+ or P1+ capacity (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/concept-data-agent)
Fabric data agents run read-only and use the requesting user's identity (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/concept-data-agent)

Fabric data agents allow up to 5 data sources, return at most 25 rows by 25 columns per answer, are English-only, don't support unstructured files, and the LLM can't be changed (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/concept-data-agent)
Fabric data agent queries fail if the data source capacity is in a different region from the agent's capacity (https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/concept-data-agent)

The Computer Use agent tool is available only in some regions, for example East US 2, Sweden Central and West Europe, but not East US (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)
The Browser Automation agent tool runs on your own Microsoft Playwright Workspaces (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry-classic/agents/whats-new)
Neither Browser Automation nor Computer Use works in network-isolated Foundry (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link)

The Foundry project endpoint is `https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>`, used by the Foundry SDK for agents, tools, evaluations and connections (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)
Microsoft Entra tokens for the Foundry project endpoint use scope `https://ai.azure.com/.default` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)

The OpenAI-compatible v1 endpoint is `https://<resource-name>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/` and works with the standard OpenAI SDKs (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)
The Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint accepts either API keys or Entra tokens with scope `https://ai.azure.com/.default` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)
The Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint accepts Microsoft Entra tokens for `https://ai.azure.com/.default` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)
An Azure OpenAI resource provides only the OpenAI-compatible v1 endpoint, while a Foundry resource provides all endpoints (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)

facts.fact: Claude models in Foundry use the Anthropic-native endpoint `https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic`, with Messages at `/anthropic/v1/messages` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)
The Foundry Anthropic endpoint works with the Anthropic SDK (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)

Foundry SDK packages: Python `azure-ai-projects` 2.x (docs require >=2.3.0; PyPI had 2.11.0 as of 2026-11-14) with `openai>=3.0.0`; JavaScript `@azure/ai-projects` 2.8.0; .NET `Azure.AI.Projects`, `Azure.AI.Projects.Agents` and `Azure.AI.Extensions.OpenAI` 2.0.0; Java `com.azure:azure-ai-projects` and `azure-ai-agents` 2.3.0 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview ; https://pypi.org/project/azure-ai-projects/)
`azure-ai-projects` is the Python package of the Foundry SDK, at 2.11.0 on PyPI as of 2026-11-14 (https://pypi.org/project/azure-ai-projects/)
The 1.x versions of the Foundry SDK packages target Foundry (classic) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)

The Azure control plane is Azure Resource Manager at `https://management.azure.com` with `api-version` query parameters; for example Foundry project connections are created with `PUT .../providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/{account}/projects/{project}/connections/{name}?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)
Azure Resource Manager is the control plane of Microsoft Azure (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)
The official Azure MCP Server is open source in `microsoft/mcp` (moved from `Azure/azure-mcp`), with source under `servers/Azure.Mcp.Server` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp)

Azure MCP Server packages are npm `@azure/mcp`, NuGet `Azure.Mcp`, PyPI `msmcp-azure`, Docker `mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sdk/azure-mcp` and the VS Code extension `ms-azuretools.vscode-azure-mcp-server` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/README.md)

Start Azure MCP Server with `npx -y @azure/mcp@latest server start`, `dotnet tool install Azure.Mcp`, `uvx --from msmcp-azure azmcp server start` or `docker run -i --rm --env-file <path> mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sdk/azure-mcp:latest` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/README.md)
In Claude Code, install the Azure MCP Server with `/plugin install azure@claude-plugins-official` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/README.md)

Azure MCP Server 2.0 went stable on 2026-04-10, adding self-hosted remote (HTTP) mode with managed-identity or On-Behalf-Of auth, US Government and 21Vianet clouds, and 276 tools across 57 services (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/azure-sdk/announcing-azure-mcp-server-2-0-stable-release)

On npm, `@azure/mcp@latest` installs a beta: the `latest` dist-tag points to `4.0.0-beta.7` (2026-11-11), so pin `@azure/mcp@3.0.0` if you need stable (https://registry.npmjs.org/@azure/mcp ; https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/releases)
The newest stable Azure MCP Server release is `3.0.0` (2026-10-12) (https://registry.npmjs.org/@azure/mcp ; https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/releases)

Azure MCP Server tools cover 50+ service namespaces, including `foundry`, `search`, `speech`, `sreagent`, `storage`, `cosmos`, `sql`, `postgres`, `kusto`, `monitor`, `keyvault`, `role`, `policy`, `quota`, `pricing`, `functionapp`, `appservice`, `aks`, `acr`, `eventgrid`, `servicebus`, `bicepschema`, `azureterraform`, `deploy`, `extension` (az and azd) and `group`/`subscription` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-mcp-server/tools/)

Azure MCP Server start options: `--mode` takes `namespace` (default), `consolidated`, `all` or `single`; plus namespace filters, `--read-only`, `--tool` to expose named tools, the transport (default `stdio`) and an option to disable elicitation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-mcp-server/tools/)

Azure MCP Server elicitation prompts the user before tools return secrets such as Key Vault values, and disabling it isn't recommended (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-mcp-server/tools/)

In local mode Azure MCP Server uses a custom credential chain in the order Environment, Visual Studio, VS Code, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, azd, then interactive browser; `AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS` pins one credential (or `prod` for non-interactive only) (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)
`AZURE_MCP_ONLY_USE_BROKER_CREDENTIAL=true` makes Azure MCP Server use WAM on Windows, and the server never stores tokens (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)

In remote mode Azure MCP Server auth is set with `--outgoing-auth-strategy`, which takes `UseOnBehalfOf` (default) or `UseHostingEnvironmentIdentity` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)
For remote Azure MCP Server the Entra app must expose scope `Mcp.Tools.ReadWrite` (delegated) or app role `Mcp.Tools.ReadWrite.All` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)
The azd templates `azmcp-obo-template` and `azmcp-foundry-aca-mi` set up remote Azure MCP Server on Azure Container Apps (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)

Azure MCP Server remote (HTTP) mode supports managed-identity auth, for example via `UseHostingEnvironmentIdentity` and the `azmcp-foundry-aca-mi` template (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/azure-sdk/announcing-azure-mcp-server-2-0-stable-release ; https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/docs/Authentication.md)

Azure MCP Server telemetry is on by default; opt out with `AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=false`, or set `AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY_MICROSOFT=false` to keep only your own Application Insights telemetry (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/blob/main/servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/README.md)

facts.fact: The Microsoft Fabric MCP Server is in public preview and built from `microsoft/mcp`, with source under `servers/Fabric.Mcp.Server` (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp)
Microsoft Fabric MCP Server version 1.8.0 was released on 2026-11-11 (https://github.com/microsoft/mcp/releases)

Foundry MCP Server (preview) is a cloud-hosted remote MCP server at `https://mcp.ai.azure.com` (streamable HTTP) giving tools for Foundry models, deployments and agents, with no infrastructure needed (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/mcp/get-started)
Foundry MCP Server uses Entra ID with On-Behalf-Of (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/mcp/get-started)
Using Foundry MCP Server requires Contributor or higher on the Foundry project (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/mcp/get-started)

Foundry agents call external remote MCP servers through the `mcp` tool with settings `server_url`, a unique `server_label`, `allowed_tools`, `require_approval` (default `always`; also `never` or per-tool lists) and `project_connection_id` for stored credentials (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Approval-required MCP calls return `mcp_approval_request`, and you answer with `mcp_approval_response` in the same conversation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Foundry agents authenticate to MCP and tool connections key-based (custom headers), with Microsoft Entra (agent identity or project managed identity), with OAuth identity passthrough (On-Behalf-Of), or unauthenticated (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)
Some MCP servers, such as the Azure DevOps MCP Server, can be added straight from the Foundry Add Tools catalog (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)
Foundry Agent Service supports A2A protocol v1.0 (GA) and v0.3 (preview), with calls in both directions (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Incoming A2A on a Foundry agent is enabled with a PATCH on the agent (`agent_card` plus `protocol_configuration.a2a`) through REST or SDK, not the portal; the base path is `.../agents/{agent}/endpoint/protocols/a2a` with cards at `.../agentCard/v1.0` and `.../agentCard/v0.3` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Callers of incoming A2A on Foundry need the `Foundry Agent Consumer` role (ID `eed3b665-ab3a-47b6-8f48-c9382fb1dad6`) at project or agent scope and a token for `https://ai.azure.com/.default` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Incoming A2A on Foundry supports only JSON-RPC for v1.0 and only text, with no SSE streaming; tasks and contexts are kept for 60 days (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Outgoing A2A from a Foundry agent uses the `A2ATool`, which needs a `RemoteA2A` project connection (for example `authType` `AgenticIdentityToken`, audience `https://ai.azure.com`) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)
The `A2ATool` is the Foundry Agent Service tool for outgoing A2A calls (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

Azure API Management can expose a managed REST API as a remote MCP server whose operations become tools at `https://<apim>.azure-api.net/<api-name>-mcp/mcp`, on Developer, Basic, Standard, Premium and the v2 tiers and in the self-hosted gateway (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/export-rest-mcp-server ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/mcp-server-overview)
APIM MCP servers support only MCP tools (no resources or prompts), and APIM workspaces aren't supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/export-rest-mcp-server)

APIM can front existing MCP servers (for example on Logic Apps, Functions or LangServe) and import A2A agent APIs; MCP servers can be managed with REST, ARM, Bicep, the Azure CLI or Terraform (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/mcp-server-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)
APIM MCP servers can be registered for discovery in Azure API Center (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/mcp-server-overview)

The APIM AI gateway applies policies `llm-token-limit`, `llm-emit-token-metric`, `llm-semantic-cache-lookup`/`llm-semantic-cache-store` and `llm-content-safety`, and gives backends load balancing (round-robin, weighted, priority, session-aware) and a circuit breaker that honors `Retry-After` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)
APIM semantic cache policies `llm-semantic-cache-lookup`/`llm-semantic-cache-store` work with Azure Managed Redis (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)
The APIM AI gateway supports OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses, Anthropic Messages (v2 tiers) and Vertex AI APIs (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)
The AI gateway is a set of Azure API Management capabilities for LLM APIs (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)

APIM's unified model API (preview) exposes a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint over many LLM backends, including Amazon Bedrock backends (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)
An AI gateway integrated into Microsoft Foundry is in preview (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)

The Azure Functions MCP extension serves streamable HTTP at `/runtime/webhooks/mcp` and deprecated SSE at `/runtime/webhooks/mcp/sse` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-mcp)

The Azure Functions MCP extension offers tool, resource and prompt triggers plus MCP Apps, in C# (isolated worker, `Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker.Extensions.Mcp`), Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Java; PowerShell and Go aren't supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-mcp)
The MCP extension turns an Azure Functions function app into a remote MCP server (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-mcp)

The Microsoft Learn MCP Server is a free, unauthenticated remote MCP server at `https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp` (streamable HTTP; a browser GET returns 405) (https://learn.microsoft.com/training/support/mcp)

Microsoft Learn MCP Server tools are `microsoft_docs_search`, `microsoft_docs_fetch` and `microsoft_code_sample_search`, and its index refreshes incrementally and fully once a day (https://learn.microsoft.com/training/support/mcp-developer-reference)
Foundry agents publish to Microsoft 365 and Teams through the Activity protocol with `azd ai agent publish` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)
Foundry IQ knowledge bases connect to Copilot Studio agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/what-is-foundry-iq)
APIM MCP servers can be consumed by Copilot Studio (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)

Foundry agent tools connect to the Fabric data agent and Fabric IQ, Azure Databricks Genie MCP (On-Behalf-Of), Microsoft Dataverse, SharePoint, Work IQ (Microsoft 365), Azure DevOps MCP and Twilio (voice channels) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/overview)

JDBC and ODBC drivers don't apply to Foundry or Agent Service, which are REST/SDK-only; SQL connectivity applies to data services such as Azure SQL and Fabric SQL endpoints (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview)

Foundry routines pair a trigger (for example `--trigger recurring --cron`) with an agent invocation through `azd ai routine` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/cli-agent-development)
Hosted agents with the Invocations protocol can receive webhooks, and Logic Apps triggers (classic) can also invoke agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents)

Install the Azure CLI on Windows with `winget install --exact --id Microsoft.AzureCLI` (64-bit by default), or use the MSI (`https://aka.ms/installazurecliwindowsx64`) or a ZIP (preview, no admin needed) (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)
The current Azure CLI version is 2.92.0 (as of 2026-11-14); update with `az upgrade` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)

Sign in to the Azure CLI with `az login` (or with a service principal, a managed identity or Cloud Shell), set the subscription with `az account set --subscription`, and get tokens with `az account get-access-token --resource <aud>` (use the `expires_on` POSIX field) (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli)
Since September 2025, MFA is required for user identities in the Azure CLI, but not for service principals or managed identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli)
The Azure CLI can sign in with a managed identity as well as a user, service principal or Cloud Shell (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli)

The Azure CLI stores credentials and extensions under `%USERPROFILE%\.azure`: the token cache is `msal_token_cache.bin` or `msal_token_cache.json`, and extensions are in `%USERPROFILE%\.azure\cliextensions` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)

Install azd on Windows with `winget install microsoft.azd`, `choco install azd` or `powershell -ex AllSigned -c "Invoke-RestMethod 'https://aka.ms/install-azd.ps1' | Invoke-Expression"` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd)
azd bundles its own GitHub CLI and Bicep CLI, and `azd update` (beta) upgrades it in place (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd)

The current azd release is 1.37.3, released on 2026-11-04/05; Windows Arm64 builds are still alpha (https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/releases ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/install-azd)

Sign in to azd with `azd auth login`, with options `--use-device-code`, `--client-id`/`--tenant-id` with `--federated-credential-provider github|azure-pipelines|oidc`, and `--managed-identity` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/reference)
azd config lives in `%USERPROFILE%\.azd\config.json`, which `AZD_CONFIG_DIR` overrides (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/reference)
Core azd commands are `azd init`, `azd up`, `azd provision`, `azd deploy` and `azd down --purge` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/developer/azure-developer-cli/reference)

facts.fact: The Azure status page at `https://azure.status.microsoft/en-us/status` covers widespread incidents only (https://azure.status.microsoft/en-us/status)
Subscription-specific Azure issues are shown in Azure Service Health in the portal, not on the public status page (https://azure.status.microsoft/en-us/status)
Azure CLI release notes are at `https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/release-notes-azure-cli` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)
azd release notes are at `https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/releases` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)
Bicep release notes are at `https://github.com/Azure/bicep/releases` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)
azurerm release notes are at `https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/releases` (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows)

Main official sample repos are `https://github.com/microsoft-foundry/foundry-samples` (hosted agents in Python and C#, infrastructure templates), `https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ai-gateway` (APIM AI gateway labs) and `https://github.com/Azure-Samples/azure-search-openai-demo` (agentic retrieval) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities)

Azure OpenAI quota is granted per subscription, per region, per model and per deployment type, in TPM, and each TPM assignment sets that deployment's rate limit (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Azure OpenAI RPM is derived from capacity units: older chat models get 6 RPM per 1,000 TPM; o3 and o4-mini get 1 RPM per 1,000 TPM; o1 gets 1 RPM per 6,000 TPM; o3-mini, o1-mini and o3-pro get 1 RPM per 10,000 TPM (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Azure OpenAI RPM is enforced over 1-second or 10-second windows, so short bursts can return 429 below the per-minute limit; for example a 600-RPM deployment throttles above 10 requests in a second (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Azure OpenAI TPM counts actual tokens, not `max_tokens`; 429 responses include `retry-after-ms`, and every response includes `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`/`-requests` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Standard deployments can get 429s below quota during temporary rate-limit cuts because Standard and Global Standard share a capacity pool; spot it when `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` is lower than the configured TPM; Provisioned (PTU) deployments avoid this (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Foundry has nine deployment types with SKU codes `GlobalStandard`, `GlobalProvisionedManaged`, `GlobalBatch`, `DataZoneStandard`, `DataZoneProvisionedManaged`, `DataZoneBatch`, `Standard`, `ProvisionedManaged` and `DeveloperTier` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)
The Foundry Developer tier is for fine-tune evaluation only: deployments expire after 24 hours and have no SLA (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)

Foundry Batch deployment tiers cost 50% less, target 24-hour turnaround and use separate enqueued quota (as of 2026-11-14) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)

Global deployment types may process inference data in any Azure region; Data Zone types stay in the US, EU (EU Data Boundary, which may include EFTA) or APAC zone; Standard and Regional Provisioned stay in the chosen geography (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)

New models arrive in the order Global, then Data Zone, then geography, and geography deployment types have no guaranteed date (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)
Azure Policy can block specific Foundry deployment SKUs (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types)

Foundry quota tiers (Tier 0 to Tier 6) set default TPM and RPM; Tier 0 (free) can't request increases; for example Tier 1 gives `gpt-4.1` GlobalStandard 1,000,000 TPM / 1,000 RPM and DataZoneStandard 300,000 TPM / 300 RPM (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/quotas-limits)

Subscriptions upgrade quota tiers automatically based on usage; opt out with `tierUpgradePolicy: NoAutoUpgrade` (preview API `2025-10-01-preview`) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/quotas-limits)

Starting after 2026-05-07 quota is moving to shared subscription-wide pools: Global Standard deployments of the same model and version share one pool across all regions, and Data Zone Standard shares one pool per data zone, beginning with Realtime Translate and Realtime Whisper with all models to follow (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/quotas-limits)

Azure OpenAI fixed limits: 30 resources per region per subscription, 32 standard deployments per resource, 128 tools or functions per `/chat/completions` request, 2,048 messages, 2,048 embedding inputs (300,000 tokens), 100,000 PTU per deployment and 10 custom headers (more causes HTTP 431) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/quotas-limits)

Azure OpenAI quota increases go through the request form `https://aka.ms/oai/stuquotarequest`, prioritized for customers using their current quota; partner and community models don't support increases, except Anthropic (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)
Viewing Azure OpenAI quota requires the `Cognitive Services Usages Reader` role at subscription scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

facts.fact: Check Azure OpenAI quota and capacity through ARM: Usages `GET .../providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/locations/{location}/usages?api-version=2024-10-01` and Model Capacities `GET .../providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/modelCapacities?api-version=2024-10-01&modelFormat=OpenAI&modelName=...&modelVersion=...` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Deleting an Azure OpenAI resource through the API with deployments still on it holds their quota for 48 hours until the resource is purged; purge the deleted resource to free it immediately (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/quota)

Non-streaming MCP tool calls from Foundry agents time out after 100 seconds; for longer work use background mode with a supported model (preview) or MCP tasks through a toolbox (preview) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Foundry agents accept only remote MCP endpoints, so local stdio servers must be hosted on Azure Container Apps (Linux amd64, stateless) or Functions (no `npx`/`uvx`, key auth only) (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Private MCP servers for Foundry agents need Standard Agent Setup with BYO VNet, and 'Invalid tool schema' errors usually come from `anyOf`/`allOf` or multi-type parameters (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/model-context-protocol)

Foundry Agent Service fixed limits that can't be raised: 128 tools per agent, 1,000 versions per agent (a terminal `UserError` beyond that), 100,000 messages per thread, 1,500,000 characters per message, 512 MB per file, 300 GB of total files and 2,000,000 tokens per vector-store file (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)

Concurrent hosted-agent sessions are capped per subscription per region at 2,000 in Canada Central, East US 2, Japan East, North Central US, South Africa North, Southeast Asia and Sweden Central and 1,000 elsewhere; exceeding it returns 429 `session_quota_exceeded` or `regional_session_quota_exceeded`, and a full delegated subnet returns `subnet_exhausted` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)

Agent tool availability differs by region and model: file search isn't available in Italy North or Brazil South, and many open and partner models (such as Llama-4-Scout and Mistral-small) support only code interpreter and file search; check the tool-by-region and tool-by-model matrices (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/limits-quotas-regions)

Network-isolated Foundry doesn't support Fabric Data Agent, Logic Apps, Browser Automation, Computer Use or Image Generation tools; Bing, web search and SharePoint still work but go over public endpoints, and tools that leave through the VNet need a project-level capability host or fail with `name or host unknown` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link)

Foundry Private Link: outbound VNet injection can't be added or changed after creation (redeploy instead); the subnet must be delegated to `Microsoft.App/environments` and be /27 or larger; don't use 172.17.0.0/16; private endpoints for BYO Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB aren't created automatically; projects created before 2026-06-25 need a public ACR for hosted-agent images (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link)

Azure AI Search indexers behind private endpoints need `executionEnvironment` set to `"Private"`, or indexing fails silently and leaves an empty index (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link)

APIM response-body logging and buffering break MCP servers: set 'Number of payload bytes to log' for Frontend Response to 0 at the All APIs scope, don't read `context.Response.Body` in MCP server policies, and use MCP Inspector 0.9.0 to test (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/export-rest-mcp-server)

Agent identities start with no permissions: assign RBAC to each agent identity by its object (principal) ID, not its application ID; migrating from shared project identities or Agent Applications to per-agent identities changes the identity, and existing role assignments don't carry over (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity ; https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)

A2A requests to Foundry with no version get preview v0.3, not v1.0; set `A2A-Version: 1.0`, use `?a2a-version=1.0` or fetch the `agentCard/v1.0` card, and if header and query string disagree the service returns HTTP 400 `version-ambiguous` (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)
A2A requests to Foundry without a version default to preview v0.3 rather than v1.0 (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint)
